plan.notes: Source: Adams State University official 'Bachelor of Arts in Psychology, Suggested 4-year Academic Plan' degree map (rev. 10/20/20, PDF linked from the official Bachelor's Degree Maps page), hand-transcribed 2026-09-30. CREDIT DISCLOSURES: (1) The map itself states no per-course credits. Per-course credits for named PSYC courses come from the current official Adams State catalog BA Psychology program page (adams.catalog.acalog.com, current catalog): PSYC 204/205/230/245/265/414/468 and 386/410/416/455/458 = 3; PSYC 211 = 4; PSYC 355 = 4; PSYC 330 = 1; PSYC 497 = 2; PSYC 498 = 3. (2) FYS 101 = 3 per the university's other official degree maps. (3) PSYC 101, all Gen Ed area slots, and Elective slots are modeled at 3 credits (standard slots); the map does not state them — actual credits depend on the course chosen (e.g., a lab science may be 4). (4) PSYC 355's co-requirement LS 225 (Library Science) is folded into the 4-credit PSYC 355 slot per the current catalog listing. (5) PSYC 496 Capstone: Internship is listed in the catalog as 1-15 variable credits; modeled at 3 for plan arithmetic — see advisor. (6) Plan bullets as transcribed total 119 credits; the catalog requires a minimum of 120 for the bachelor's. Map legend: * = offered Fall & Spring; + = requires Statistics; ^ = requires Statistics and Research Methods. The map notes the major provides 23 upper-level credits and students need 19 more for the 42 upper-division credits required to graduate. The map is the research-capstone track (PSYC 497/498); an internship capstone (PSYC 496) is the alternative. This plan does not guarantee timely graduation — check with an advisor.
